data.body:
Fixed and superseded by story affe-2b42-4ee4-4e12 (closed), via ticket 7ab3-9df0-7a90-4ffd — merged 693a6bf41.

Your repro is now a regression test. Blocking-link comparability no longer keys on ticket TYPE TIER; it is structural. A task T and a story S that are both direct children of epic E are SIBLINGS, so `T depends_on S` records exactly as requested — no escalation, and the epic gains nothing. The chain-root fallback at the old _hierarchy.py:93 that produced `E depends_on S` is deleted along with _TYPE_TIER and its three helpers.

Both halves of your report are addressed:
- the epic no longer gains a dependency on its own child — enforced in the resolver itself (is_redundant is now recomputed from the RESOLVED pair), so add_dependency, the `link --dry-run` preview and the standalone resolve path all inherit it;
- the requested T->S edge is now actually written, which your report noted was silently lost.

Covered by test_resolve_hierarchy_link_task_and_story_siblings_link_directly and test_add_dependency_task_to_sibling_story_writes_the_requested_edge, the latter asserting both that the requested edge exists and that no epic-to-child edge was created.

The workaround you recorded on epic 8fc2-0306-a9a0-4864 (retyping children to story, then unlinking the spurious epic->child edge) is no longer needed; retyping in particular is now a no-op for link resolution.

Legacy edges already on disk were repaired separately under 9ad7-d5a2-a664-4827: 18 found on this tracker, 12 repaired, 8 residual and provably inert (every endpoint closed, so none can reach ready/next-batch).

One part of your report is NOT fully resolved and is recorded as follow-up on the doctor epics: the "Silent" impact. The redirect record is printed by add_dependency, but rebar.link() calls link_core(..., quiet=True) (src/rebar/_lib_writes.py:615) which discards stdout, so library and MCP callers still get a silent substitution when a cross-subtree link IS escalated. Escalation is now correct; its visibility on the MCP path is not.
